What insight do you want from this question?
To start — could you tell me your role, the kind of organisation you're with, and where you're based?
Open: role + org type (practitioner / funder / researcher / government / civil society / philanthropy / academia / edtech / social entrepreneur) + country (state if India)
Persona, organisation type and geographic reach.
Has InvokED shifted how you think about collective action, education leadership, or system change?
Tap: No change / Somewhat shifted / Significantly shifted
Always, once. Branch on the answer above.

If Somewhat / Significantly → What's the one idea or belief that changed for you, and what prompted it?

If No change → What would have made a real difference for you?
Magnitude of the shift and the substance behind it.
Since InvokED, has anything concrete come out of it — a collaboration, a pilot, a partnership, or a conversation you took forward?
Always, three times. Branch every probe on the answer above.

PROBE 1 — If Yes / In progress → Who is it with, and what are you doing together?
If No → Is there a connection or idea from InvokED you'd still like to take forward, and what's holding it up?

PROBE 2 — If Yes / In progress → Was that someone you met at InvokED, or someone you already knew? (tap: met at InvokED / already knew / a mix)
If No → What would make it easier to act on it?

PROBE 3 — If Yes / In progress → What's come out of it so far, or what do you expect it to lead to?
If No → Is there anyone you met at InvokED you're still in touch with, even informally?

If the main answer already named the partner and the work, skip probe 1 and run probes 2 and 3.
Collaboration rate, partner names, type, and the full action story (who + what + outcome). Probe 2 establishes whether the partner was met at InvokED or already known.
Has any of this shaped how your organisation works — a decision, a programme, an approach? And what changed?
Tap: Not at all / Moderately / Significantly, plus one line of open text — both in the same turn
Looking ahead — would you take part in InvokED again? And what would make staying connected through the year genuinely worth your time?
Tap: Yes / Maybe / No, plus open (forums / online problem-solving / thematic meet-ups / knowledge resources + theme)
Retention intent and the year-round engagement offer.

Last one, and it's the big one — 'future readiness' is a phrase everyone uses and almost no one defines the same way. In your work, what does it actually mean? And what are you doing that moves it forward?
Open, two parts in one turn: (a) their definition of future readiness, (b) what they are concretely doing about it. Expect 2–4 sentences.
How senior education leaders define future readiness and how they are contributing to it.
Maximum 10 turns per conversation. A probe counts as a turn.
Only Q2 (1 probe) and Q3 (3 probes) may probe. Q1, Q4, Q5 and Q6 never spawn a follow-up.
Never re-ask something the respondent has already volunteered.
Editions attended (1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / All 5) is pre-filled from the registrant record, or collected as a tap on the post-close screen. It is not a conversational turn.
The post-close screen collects, all optional: photo upload · willingness to share a written or video story · Shikshagraha Awards nomination or self-nomination · best contact for follow-up.
